subject.title: refactor(qa): migrate Matrix scenarios into QA Lab

question: Should QA Lab access Matrix through a generic runner/plugin seam with the Gateway lifecycle change reviewed separately, or should OpenClaw intentionally accept Matrix-named Plugin SDK methods and the global restart behavior in this migration?
rationale: Repository policy favors plugin-agnostic SDK boundaries, while accepting the current shape creates a durable API contract and changes process-wide channel lifecycle behavior that automation cannot choose on maintainers’ behalf.

options.title: Restore generic boundaries
options.body: Keep Matrix calls inside QA Lab or its package facade, separate the Gateway lifecycle change, and authorize only the narrowed dependency move.

options.title: Approve the expanded contract
options.body: Explicitly accept the Matrix-specific SDK surface and global restart semantics, with compatibility documentation and broader lifecycle proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Restore generic boundaries
recommendation.body: Keep Matrix calls inside QA Lab or its package facade, separate the Gateway lifecycle change, and authorize only the narrowed dependency move.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the merged foundation and current migration stack and can coordinate the boundary decision with the relevant reviewers.
